etymologies.etymologyHTML: From under- +‎ -wear. Compare Dutch ondergoed, German Unterwäsche, Swedish underkläder.

definitions.definition: Clothes worn next to the skin, underneath outer clothing.

quote.text: Don't scratch and bite, my little bear, you'll soon need bigger underwear.

quote.citation: 2016 June 30, Stefan Hertmans, War and Turpentine‎[1], Random House, →ISBN, →OCLC, page 202:
quote.text: As a couple of soldiers sing a dirty song, he loses sight of the edge of the stage and falls off in the middle of his dance like a seasoned slapstick artist, his white legs in the air and his filthy underwear visible to all.

definitions.definition: (colloquial) Underpants (boxers, briefs, panties, etc) and often bras.

quote.citation: 2006, Toni L. Meilleur, Tournament of Fire:
quote.text: “A thong,” she answered him breathlessly. Now completely turned on by the fact that his man was sniffing her underwear and grinning like a tiger that took down its prey. That is if tigers could smile and still look sexy.
